changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For membership businesses that report churn to their board: lead with involuntary churn, not payments. Example: 'Part of your churn is members who never meant to leave: their card just failed. We get them back with automatic retries and updated cards.'
changes.why: The deal began as a board-level churn problem and only became a payments problem once the failed-card bucket, 'members who never meant to leave', turned out to be much bigger than expected, so recovery should be positioned as the fix for that churn number.

changes.change: New proof offer for the first meeting, aimed at the controller as well as the champion: 'Send us one month of your failed renewals. We'll show you which ones usually come back with a retry or an updated card. Your file, not our average.' Get the result to finance before the contract goes to them.
changes.why: The contract sat with the controller for two weeks. He had been silent for two meetings, asked for the spreadsheet after the own-file session, and the deal was signed four days later.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: Stop leading with this for prospects who run their front desks inside studio management software, until we can demo the reader live inside their software. Lead with online membership recovery, and present the front desk as a later phase through the partner integration.
changes.why: The unified-commerce pitch was heard as 'is that the readers?'. We couldn't show it live because it runs through a partner integration, and the win stopped at that line: memberships signed, studios deferred with no date.

changes.change: For prospects whose incumbent counters with front-desk hardware and a longer contract, answer early with a staged path: 'Start with online membership billing and failed-renewal recovery now; your front desks can stay where they are for phase one.'
changes.why: The incumbent countered with a terminal bundle on a longer contract, the buyer's questions shifted to readers, contract term and exit cost, and what they actually signed was online memberships first, with the studios as phase two.
